div.head: Rect 14
div.ab: [14] Be sceaphyrdan. Sceaphyrdes riht is, þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta [d]ingan to Middanwintra ⁊ I lamb of geares geogeðe ⁊ I belflys ⁊ his heorde meolc VII niht æfter emnihtes dæge ⁊ blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor.

Pastoris ouium rectum est, ut habeat dingiam XII noctium in natali Domini et I agnum de iuuentute hornotina et I belflis (id est timpani uellus) et lac gregis sui VII noctibus ante equinoctium et blede (id est cuppam) plenam mesguii de siringia tota estate.

Be sceap hyrdan . Sceaphyrdes riht is þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta ðingan to middanwintra . 7. i. lamb of geares geogeðe . 7 i belflys . 7 his heorde meolc . vii . niht æfter emnihtes dæge 7 blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor .

Be sceaphyrdan Sceaphyrdes riht is þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta dingan to middanwintra, and I lamb of geares geogeðe, and I belflys, and his heorde meolc VII niht æfter emnihtes dæge, and blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor.

Von Schafhirten. Des Schafhirten Gebühr ist, dass er den Dung erhalte von den Zwölf Nächten zu Weihnachten und ein Lamm vom Jungvieh des Jahres und ein Glockenflies und die Milch seiner Herde 7 Tage lang nach dem Tage der [Herbst-] Nachtgleiche und eine Schale voll Molken oder Buttermilch den ganzen Sommer [täglich].

Of the shepherd. The shepherd's due is that he receive the dung of the Twelve Nights at Christmas [the dung dropped by the lord's flock from 25 December to 6 January] and one lamb of the year's young and one bell-fleece [the fleece of the bell-wether] and the milk of his flock for 7 days after the [autumn] equinox, and a bowl full of whey or buttermilk [daily] all summer.

Concerning the shepherd The shepherd’s right is that he has twelve night’s [worth of] dung at mid-winter, and one lamb from the year’s young, and the fleece of one bell-wether [the lead ram of the flock], and his flock’s milk [for] seven nights after the equinox, and a bowl full of whey or sour milk [for the] entire summer.

Regarding the Shepherd It is the right of the shepherd to have twelve nights’ worth of dung at midwinter, and one lamb from the year’s young, and the fleece of one bellwether, and the flock’s milk for seven nights after the autumn equinox, and a bowlful of whey or buttermilk for the entire summer.
div.note: B reads ‘ði.’; Liebermann prints ‘[d]ingan’ (corrected from the Quadripartitus and Gerefa 9). B's ‘geogeðe’ is corrected from ‘geoðeðe’. The Quadripartitus read ‘ær’ (before) for ‘æfter’. Liebermann compares Rect 16.

Ende Sept. entwöhnen sich die dann 2 Monate alten Lämmer bereits; Ende März wären die Mütter erst trächtig.—Hier melken wohl Männer, wie in Essex in späterem MA.; Round Victoria county hist. Essex I 373

At the end of Sept. the lambs, then 2 months old, are already weaning themselves; at the end of March the ewes would only just be with young.—Here the milking is probably done by men, as in Essex in the later Middle Ages; Round Victoria county hist. Essex I 373

Schafmilch ergab im MA. in Essex Butter und Käse; ebd., auch bei Ælfric Colloq. Sind also Molken und Buttermilch hier vom Schafe?—Nordisch heisst syra: ‘sour whey, saure Molken’, was Sweet gegen andere Forscher als Bed. von syring annimmt. ‘Saure Milch’ (Leo) oder ‘abgerahmte Milch’ (Schmid) passt nicht; laut 16, wo nochmals erwähnt, ist syring etwas nach Butter- und Käsebereitung noch Übriges. So Andrews 220, Toller s. v.: die entfettete, nach Buttern übrige säuerliche Flüssigkeit, noch heute Getränk auf dem Lande, das dialektisch sour milk heisst; Wright Dial. dict. V 633

In the Middle Ages ewes' milk yielded butter and cheese in Essex; ibid., also in Ælfric Colloq. Are the whey and buttermilk here, then, from the sheep?—In Norse syra means ‘sour whey, saure Molken’, which Sweet, against other scholars, takes to be the meaning of syring. ‘Sour milk’ (Leo) or ‘skimmed milk’ (Schmid) does not fit; according to 16, where it is mentioned again, syring is something still left over after butter- and cheese-making. So Andrews 220, Toller s. v.: the sourish liquid, with the fat removed, left over after churning, still drunk in the country today and called sour milk in dialect; Wright Dial. dict. V 633
